Absorb a divide's sliver parts into the neighbour they share the most boundary with

Source: R/absorb_divide_slivers.R
dot-absorb_divide_slivers.Rd

construct_agg_divides unions each aggregate's member catchments, so an aggregate whose members are not spatially contiguous gets a genuinely multi-part divide. Most of that multi-part-ness is not a real disjoint catchment: on CONUS, 1,192 of 1,300 multi-part divides have a second part under 1% of the divide (median 900 m2). Those are slivers left by clipping, snapping and union arithmetic.

Nothing downstream reduces them. dissolve_multipart_divides runs in reconcile_divides, which is BEFORE the aggregation that creates the fragmentation, and hfutils::clean_gpkg_layer(gap_fill_area = ) fills holes BETWEEN divides, a divide's own second part is an owned polygon, not a gap, so it is never a gap-fill candidate.

This pass moves each qualifying sliver into the adjacent divide it shares the most boundary with, which is the divide that land most plausibly drains to. It is area-conserving by construction: the polygon changes owner, it is never dropped. That distinction matters, the dissolve-and-drop approach used at the refactor phase would forfeit 285 km2 nationally, and for a genuinely disjoint divide it would discard a real catchment.

Deliberately conservative. A part must be BOTH absolutely small (min_part_km2) and small relative to its own divide (max_part_frac) before it is eligible, so the ~53 divides whose second part is a substantial fraction of a real catchment keep their multi-part geometry. A sliver with no adjacent divide is kept as well: carrying a multi-part divide is better than losing the land.

Usage

.absorb_divide_slivers(
  div,
  min_part_km2 = 0.01,
  max_part_frac = 0.01,
  min_shared_m = 1,
  flowlines = NULL
)

Arguments

div

Divides sf.

min_part_km2

Absolute ceiling on an absorbable part, km2. Default 0.01 (1 hectare), which covers 1,194 of the 1,300 CONUS cases.

max_part_frac

Ceiling on an absorbable part as a fraction of its own divide's total area. Default 0.01.

min_shared_m

Minimum shared boundary with the recipient, metres. A part touching only at a point would union into a still-disjoint polygon.

Value

A list with div (repaired layer), n_absorbed, n_kept (eligible slivers with no usable neighbour), area_moved_km2, and n_multi_before / n_multi_after.
